topic: Water use by district under summer restrictions
decision: where to focus enforcement if the summer watering restrictions are extended

columns.litres_per_household_day: average litres per household per day
columns.target_lphd: district target under restrictions, litres per household per day (20% below April-May)
columns.enforcement_notices: warning notices issued for breaking restrictions
columns.smart_meter_pct: percentage of homes with smart meters

findings.text: July rainfall was about half the normal amount.
Seven of the eight districts cut use per household by 17% to 27% after restrictions began on 1 June. Hillcrest cut by only 4%.
Enforcement notices peaked in July, at about 1,240 across the valley.
About 60% of homes have smart meters.
Hillcrest households used 414 litres a day from June to September, against a target of 342 litres (20% below their April-May level).
August was the hottest month, averaging 25 °C.
Hillcrest's water meters were replaced in July, and the new meters read about 8% higher than the old ones. Allowing for that, Hillcrest's cut is about 9%, still well short of the 20% target.
Total water use across the valley fell 20% after restrictions began.
Orchard has the lowest use per household (218 litres a day under restrictions).

main.gist: Hillcrest barely cut its water use while the other districts cut about a fifth

caveat.gist: Hillcrest's new meters read about 8% higher

facts.q: By what percentage did Hillcrest cut water use per household after the restrictions, and roughly what was the cut in the other districts?
